---
title: "Cite this course"
subtitle: "How to reference Molecules & Models in a paper, a syllabus or a thesis."
---

If this course helped your work or your teaching, please cite it. The repository contains a machine-readable [`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/Awguhst/MolModels/blob/main/CITATION.cff) that GitHub renders as a "Cite this repository" button.

## Plain text

> Rostislav Rusev (2026). *Molecules & Models: a practical path from data science to cheminformatics and bioinformatics* (version 0.1.0). https://YOUR-USER.github.io/molecules-and-models/

## BibTeX

```bibtex
@misc{molecules_and_models_2026,
  author       = {Rusev, Rostislav},
  title        = {Molecules \& Models: a practical path from data science to cheminformatics and bioinformatics},
  year         = {2026},
  version      = {0.1.0},
  howpublished = {\url{https://YOUR-USER.github.io/molecules-and-models/}},
  note         = {Open educational resource. Text CC BY 4.0, code MIT.}
}
```

## Citing a single episode

Give the episode number and title and the date you accessed it, for example:

> Rostislav Rusev (2026). "2.3 Evaluating models honestly", in *Molecules & Models*. https://YOUR-USER.github.io/molecules-and-models/part-1-foundations/ch02-ml-fundamentals/03-evaluating-models.html (accessed 31 October 2026).

The last-updated date at the bottom of every page comes from the git history of that page.

## Citing the datasets

Please also cite the original data when you use it in your own work; the full references are in the [data README](https://github.com/Awguhst/MolModels/blob/main/data/README.md) and on the [About](about.html) page.

Text and figures: [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Code (including the notebooks): MIT. Attribution to the course URL is sufficient.
